newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Edison nuke seen in startup Monday.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Edison nuke seen in startup Monday.

text.p: Detroit Edison, operator of the 1,116 megawatt (MW) Fermi 2 nuclear power plant in Monroe County, Mich., expected to begin startup of the plant on Monday, a company spokeswoman said.
However it will likely be several days before the unit resumes electricity production, spokeswoman Mary Kay Bean said Monday.

"By midday we expect to startup and tomorrow we will resume testing of the turbine," Bean said, adding "depending on the outcome of the turbine test we will be able to increase power (and synchronize to the electricity grid)."
A new turbine was installed during a maintenance and refueling outage which began Sept 27, 1996.
Detroit Edison, a subsidiary of DTE Energy Corp, owns and operates the Fermi plant.
